evidence:
Graded surface: 2 gates (render authenticated_render; constraints server_backed_local_application), 16 functional binary criteria, 5 polish binary criteria, 4 visual likert criteria (27 total). I walked each against the reference.

(1) Functional 16/16 and constraints gate: the scripted golden harness (qc/repairs/kittle-2026-10-08/tests/functional.cjs) follows each criterion's legs in listed order on one database, with a real process kill/restart (restart-pids.json) before persistence. golden-run.log (sha256 23943bf8...) records 'gate_constraints PASS', all 16 functional ids PASS, 'persistence PASS', 'polish_refusal_in_place PASS', exit 0; functional-before/after.json show every result true and dialogs []. Index hashes for these artifacts and for the frozen solution bytes re-verified. I read the script against the criteria: it exercises the hard legs that quote seeded figures/boundaries (exactly-7-day 'Boundary note' gone vs one-second-younger 'Rent review meeting moved' kept, 8-day 'Probate estimate' and its '2,400' version deleted on 7-day shortening, held executor message kept, 'Insurer letter' disappearing on hold release, 'notice recieved' version not searchable, transcript header '2026-05-12 11:00'), idempotent double replay (client_key), same-timestamp A/B/C order across thread/search/transcript, stale edit 409 with typed text kept, cross-role replays refused (403/404/409), wall added live within 10 s, unread counts in two contexts with deleted message excluded, live updates preserving draft/reply target/scroll (<40 px), and nested replies depth [1,2,3,1]. Where the script used the API instead of UI (Dev's mentions list via /api/mentions), the UI route exists (index.html:31 Mentions link, :92-95 mentions-view; app.js:511-520 openMentions renders the same /api/mentions data). Where it asserted only a status (the 'plain not-available answer' legs), server.js:21 NOT_AVAILABLE='Not available.' is returned at server.js:335/342/346/516 and the transcript page at :496.

(2) Render gate, polish and visual (not covered by the 8 Oct run, so I measured them on the frozen bytes): pre-sign-in page text was only 'KITTLE & ROWE / Matter chat / Email / Password / Sign in' (no private data); wrong password shows "That email and password don't match an account." inside the sign-in form box (#signin-error y=541 within form y=258..642) and the polish refusal leg also passed in the golden after a 10 s wait; gwen signs in and M-11 shows 9 messages, no page errors. timer_label: '#matter-timer' reads 'Messages disappear after 7 days' directly under the M-11 title (same x=300), visible without a menu. hold_mark: executor message '.hold-badge' 'On hold' visible without hover. phone_matter: at 390x844 documentElement.scrollWidth = innerWidth = 390 on M-11 and M-13, composer visible at y=705 and typeable. transcript_print: M-11 transcript is 760 px max width, author/time in a separate .meta line above each body, replies indented 24 px per depth, 0 buttons/inputs/forms. Visual screenshots show a clear selected-matter state in the sidebar, a calm pill 'On hold' badge and amber timer notice beside the title, a document-like transcript heading block, and a phone layout with clean wrapping and readable hold mark; plausibly 4-5 on each likert anchor.

Conclusion: every gated and scored criterion is satisfiable by the reference; I found no criterion the reference cannot pass (no P0 per quality-checks.md #18).

Risk is true because required runtime evidence is missing, not because of a defect: there is no full configured judge run (claude-code + task.toml model, individual-mode functional, Playwright MCP, restart_app) on this candidate, so the Oracle score and LLM-judge interpretation of multi-leg criteria (e.g. scroll 'has not jumped', unread line placement, 'within about ten seconds' waits, 16 x 550 s individual-mode budget per functional/judge.toml:79-84 'Not yet measured against a judge run') remain unmeasured. The 8 Oct harness also mounted projects/kittle-matter-chat/solution, not the frozen copy; byte identity rests on the evidence index hashes (which do match the frozen files), and its browser image was cw-editor-verifier:current rather than an image built from tests/Dockerfile. Scripted golden and my probe are not an Oracle grade; I claim no Oracle, model or portal score.

Adversarial checks: a plausible broken app that would still pass row 18 is not this row's concern (row 18 is reference-side), but I confirmed the reference is not passing through leniency of the script: e.g. the script asserts literal '<img'/'<script>' text in thread, quote, search snippet and escaped transcript HTML, and 0 img/script elements. A conforming alternative that could fail is a row 27 question; for the reference itself, the only judge-dependence I see is timing/scroll interpretation, covered by the risk above.
